Performers
Felix Slatkin (first violin; Hollywood String Quartet), Paul Shure (second violin; Hollywood String Quartet), Paul Robyn (viola; Hollywood String Quartet), Eleanor Aller (cello; Hollywood String Quartet), Alvin Dinkin (second viola), Kurt Reher (second cello) Documented

The quartet’s four members are supplemented by Dinkin and Reher. The source does not identify a conductor; none is invented.

[3] [2] [5] [6]
Work version
Original version for two violins, two violas and two cellos; one continuous work divided across two LP sides. Documented

The break between bars 228 and 229 is an editorial score/audio inference: side 1 ends with the E♭-minor-to-B♭ link on score p. 25; side 2 begins with the D major Sehr breit und langsam on p. 26. Not the 1917 or 1943 string-orchestra arrangement.

[2] [3] [9]
Recorded
21–⁠22 August 1950 Documented

These are recording dates, independently distinguished from the 1950 release year and 2021 transfer.

[3]
Place
Hollywood, California Documented

The archive establishes the city, not a specific studio or room.

[3]
Label
Capitol Records — Capitol Classics Documented[4] [5] [6]
Catalogue
L-8118; mono 10-inch LP, issued 1950 Documented

The later P-8304 reissue is not the source carrier used here.

[4] [5] [6]
Matrix, take, sides
Side 1; printed label suffix (L-8118) Y Documented

This is the observed printed side identification, not a claimed session matrix or take. Runout inscriptions and take numbers are not established.

[5]
Transfer
Internet Archive; ripping operator associate-johnmark-layos Documented

Separate from original Capitol production and later reissue credits.

[1]
Transfer date
19 November 2021 Documented

ripping_date 20211119100224. Sleeve-scan and upload dates are not treated as the sound-transfer date.

[1]
Processing
Technics SL-1200MK5 with Audio-⁠Technica AT95e cartridge → RDL EZ-PH1 preamplifier → Focusrite Scarlett 2i2; ArchiveCD 2.2.57lp; Internet Archive MP3 derivative. Documented

Both side ripping notes say “scratchy disc”. FLAC comments identify SoX processing but do not establish restoration settings; scratch-sensitive onset counts are not used as musical pulse evidence.

[1]
Composition rights
The original sextet score was published in 1905; its early-publication public-domain basis in the United States is separate from rights in later editions or arrangements. Inferred, not documented

This record contains instrumental music, not a sung or recited translation of Dehmel’s poem. No later editorial score or translation licence is asserted.

[7] [9]
Recording rights
EU territorial phonogram-term basis: first lawful publication in 1950, before 1963. US recording status not established. Documented

Programme rule 3; the Arnold Schönberg Center independently identifies the 1950 original issue. No Creative Commons licence is claimed for the Archive transfer.

[4] [10]

Hollywood String Quartet with Alvin Dinkin and Kurt Reher; recorded in Hollywood, 21–⁠22 August 1950. Capitol L-8118 (1950); LP transfer supplied by Internet Archive. EU territorial recording-term basis; US status not established. Rights statement

  1. Internet Archive: Capitol L-8118 LP transfer — Metadata, disc1 MP3/FLAC files, ripping notes and digitisation lineage. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  2. Capitol L-8118 original sleeve and label OCR — Six named performers, original-version statement, composer’s programme note and label’s personal-supervision credit. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  3. Arnold Schönberg Audio Archive: Hollywood String Quartet recording 47 — Hollywood, California, 21–⁠22 August 1950; all six performers. Reissue production entries are not assumed to describe the original session or this transfer.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  4. Arnold Schönberg Audio Archive: Capitol L 8118 — Record 870: mono 10-inch LP, release 1950, programme notes by Arnold Schoenberg. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  5. Capitol L-8118 side-one label — Label visibly reads SIDE 1 and (L-8118) Y; six performer names. Runout details are not transcribed.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  6. Capitol L-8118 side-two label — Label visibly reads SIDE 2 and (L-8118) Z; six performer names. Runout details are not transcribed.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  7. Arnold Schönberg Center: Verklärte Nacht, Op. 4, original sextet catalogue — Composition September–1 December 1899; premiere 18 March 1902; first publication 1905, Dreililien-⁠Verlag, plate 345. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  8. Therese Muxeneder: Transfigured Night, Op. 4, with Schoenberg’s 1950 analysis — Poem and five-part outline; Payerbach; Dehmel letter of 12 December 1912; original sextet versus 1917/1943 orchestral versions; composer’s theme examples. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  9. Verklärte Nacht, Dreililien 1905 sextet score, composer’s copy E1 — Visually inspected pp. 2–⁠3, 12–⁠13, 24–⁠27, 44–⁠45, 50–⁠51. Image index identifies bars 204–⁠228 on pp. 24–⁠25 and bars 229–⁠250 on pp. 26–⁠27; final page ends at bar 418.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  10. Directive 2011/77/EU amending the term of phonogram protection — Article 1(2) and 1(3): term and transitional applicability on 1 November 2013. Accessed 2026-10-17.
